newsitem.title: USA: CME feeder cattle end mostly higher, Aug sets high.
newsitem.headline: CME feeder cattle end mostly higher, Aug sets high.

text.p: CME feeder cattle futures ended mostly higher on strong fundamental factors but profit taking pared gains, particularly in the August contract after a fresh contract high was posted in that month, traders said.
Lower prices paid for cash cattle this week so far, compared with last week weighed on nearby live cattle futures.

Feeder cattle ended 0.050 cent a lb lower to 0.800 higher with only August off at 80.900 cents after setting a new contract high early of 81.825. Live cattle closed 0.400 cent per lb lower to 0.400 higher with August off most at 63.525.
Lower corn futures and higher cash had supported feeders before the profit taking developed, traders said.

Another decline in corn futures and 39-month highs in the latest CME feeder cattle index boosted feeders to a new high early and kept back months supported late. Profit taking developed in nearbys with sell stops touched off in August before demand was again evident late, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.20 at $80.87 per cwt, the highest level since April 18, 1994.
Refco, Rosenthal Collins and ADM Investor Services notably bought August feeders early before selling by R.J. O'Brien and ADM Investor Services sold, traders said.
RBH sold late fall Cargill Investor Services bought. Cargill also spread long November feeders/short April live cattle, pit sources said.
Reports that packers were able to buy cattle at southern-Plains-area feedlots at $62 per cwt, down $1 from last week, added to early pressure in live cattle futures.

Sliding boxed beef values will likely keep packer bids down, traders noted, and feedlots appear more willing to take the bids with more cattle becoming market ready in the near term and demand for beef seen light the rest of the summer, traders said.
USDA reported boxed beef cut-out values slipped $0.43 to $0.63 per cwt at midday Monday, with 72 loads reported sold.

E.D.& F. Man, Dean Witter and Goldman Sachs sold August late after scattered fund selling early. R.J. O'Brien was an early buyer. In live cattle options, commission house sold August 64 calls and puts. Commercials sold the October 64/70 strangle and October 62/66 straddle, pit sources said.

Early gains in boneless beef and trimmings futures were pared after meeting selling interest at 96.00 cents, basis August boneless. E.D.&F. Man and ADM Investor Services bought August boneless early while Lind-Waldock and Term Commodities sold at the high, traders said. Lightly traded deferred boneless contracts posted new contract highs and both August and February trimmings set new highs on the early advance.
Boneless beef closed up 0.30 to 2.00 cents with August up the least at 94.80 cents. Trimmings were up 0.40 to 0.10 with August up 0.20 at 44.30 cents.
